record.name: Sri Lanka
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. Cabinet approved implementation of Sri Lanka's national AI strategy on 26 August 2024. In August 2026 the deputy minister described establishing a National AI Institute as a top priority plan for the ministry; the announcement does not state its remit.

next_check.reason: Routine re-check on a two-year rotation of states with no reported plans.

partial.scope: Negative-status confidence, preserved query provenance, national/official-language search coverage and source-independence audit; this is not a full recheck of all record fields.

Reassessed negative confidence under the revised rule using saved research. Primary governance evidence and English and Sinhala queries are recorded, but the proposed National AI Institute's mandate remains unresolved. No new search or full recheck.
Attempted preservation of cited source copies and checked saved-copy hashes; failures remain in source access notes. This source-evidence work is not a full factual recheck of the record.

Reassessed status confidence under the evidence-only rule and kept it low; the recorded Sinhala query lists the same results as the English query, so an independent national-language search is not shown. Partial check; the last full-check date is unchanged.

Re-ran searches in English, Sinhala and Tamil for a government-designated institute that evaluates advanced models, or a commitment, proposal or study naming one. No qualifying institute or commitment was identified. The Sinhala and Tamil queries returned results different from the English ones. The ministry pages on the National AI Institute stakeholder session could not be read (empty JavaScript application). Raised confidence to medium under the status-confidence rule: recorded queries in English and a national or official language, and cited primary governance evidence consistent with no qualifying institute. Partial check; the last full-check date is unchanged.

check.language_note: The recorded si query uses a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. Preserved result batches, using 1-based positions in check.searches: LK-search = searches 1, 2 (en, si). Each multi-query batch has only a combined returned result set; its source_ids cannot be attributed to individual queries. Historical query dates are recorded as 17 October 2026 in the phase6 search-boundary ledger. On 24 October 2026 the record was searched again in English, Sinhala and Tamil; the result links of each query were matched against registered sources in the same way.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: Two substantively independent evidence origins were not established. Multiple pages from one owner, mirrors, reports of the same underlying announcement and general regional coverage are not counted as independent corroboration.
check.governance_note: The Cabinet record approves implementation of the national AI strategy. The ministry separately calls a National AI Institute a top priority; a July 2026 news report of the deputy minister's remarks describes it as strengthening capacity in AI research, ethics and policymaking. The inaccessible archived strategy copy is not relied upon.

record.notes: The Cabinet decision dated 26 August 2024 approved implementation of the national AI strategy. Searches covered indexed public English and Sinhala sources for a government-designated AI safety institute with a remit to evaluate advanced models. A July 2026 news report of the deputy minister's remarks says the planned National AI Institute would strengthen local capacity in AI research, ethics and policymaking; no remit to evaluate advanced models was found.

sources.title: “Countries like ours deserve a seat at the table where AI rules are written” - Dy Minister

excerpts.text: the Government plans to establish a National AI Institute in the near future to strengthen local capacity in AI research, ethics, and policymaking.

Furthermore, the Deputy Minister stated that establishing a National AI Institute—backed by sovereign digital infrastructure strengthened through projects like DIGIECON 2030 and SLUDI—is a top priority plan for the ministry.
